To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the specific gravity of the particles in a mixture is more important than the diameter of the particles in determining where and when particles are deposited and transported.

the sediment transport and deposition of nonuniform sediments is controlled by particle size and density, and that the transport of nonuniform sedimens is controlled by the size and density of the particles with the smaller specific gravity.
the specific gravity of sediment particles is a more important factor in the deposition of heterogeneous sediment mixtures than particle size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of sediment type and slope on the transport and deposition processes.
the transport and deposition processes that occur when overland flow transports and deposits natural sediment on concave slopes.
the effects of sediment heterogeneity on the transport and deposition processes of sediment on a slope.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sediment deposited on concave slopes has a higher proportion of larger particles than the sediment transported by flow.
sediment transport and deposition on a concave slope is a function of the specific gravity of the sediment.
the sediment yield from a concave overland-flow slope is not uniform in size, shape, or density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a heterogeneous sediment mixture behaves as though it were a mixture of homogeneous sediments with the larger particles behaving as though they were the smaller ones.
the sediment yield from a concave slope depends on the sediment size, specific gravity, slope, and flow discharge.
the deposition of sediment on concave slopes depends on the specific gravity and diameter of the sediment and the slope gradient and length.
The main takeaway from our work is that

sediment transport and deposition is not uniform on concave slopes and that the nonuniformity of sediment deposition is a result of the nonuniformity in sediment properties and the nonuniformity on the concave slope.
sediment transport and deposition on concave slopes is a complex process.
the specific gravity of particles is a critical factor in determining the distribution of sediment on a concave slope, especially in a mixture of particles with different specific gravities.
